summary: The bill amends the FTC Act to bar deceptive recyclable, compostable, or reusable claims on consumer-product packaging unless backed by third-party certification, qualified by local program availability, and free of misleading resin codes, with FTC guidance and nationwide preemption of differing state rules.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the FTC Act to regulate environmental marketing claims on packaging and directs the FTC to issue guidance and enforce provisions. No appropriations, new spending programs, or fiscal authorizations are included. It has no bearing on government spending levels.
The legislation contains no tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures of any kind.
The bill addresses packaging claims for consumer products and has no connection to healthcare delivery, insurance, or medical services.
No provisions relate to firearms, ammunition, or gun regulations.
The bill does not address immigration, visas, border policy, or related enforcement.
No content pertains to reproductive health services or abortion access.
The legislation makes no reference to defense spending, military procurement, or national security budgets.

The bill establishes federal standards and third-party certification requirements for recyclable, compostable, and reusable packaging claims, prohibits deceptive environmental marketing, requires FTC guidance developed with EPA input, and preempts differing state laws. This directly regulates environmental claims to prevent greenwashing and promote accurate information about product lifecycle impacts, constituting a moderate expansion of environmental standards and consumer protections in this domain.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net benefits.
The bill has no relation to schools, education funding, or school choice policies.
No content addresses controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.
The legislation creates civil enforcement authority for the FTC but does not alter criminal penalties, sentencing, or policing practices.
The bill does not modify tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export rules.
No fiscal or deficit-related provisions are present.
The legislation contains no provisions concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No foreign assistance or international aid measures are included.
The bill does not address voting access, election administration, or voter ID requirements.
No provisions regulate data privacy, technology platforms, or digital oversight.
The legislation does not affect worker protections, collective bargaining, or union rights.
No content relates to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination laws.
